rules_text:
Rules summary Remember When ... is a family party game for 3-6 players, ages 8 and up. Note that the game is extremely language dependent, as essentially a storytelling game, in English. The players represent retired super heroes and reformed super villains who have gotten together, years later, to reminisce about their earlier adventures. But, as always happens at occasions like this, each is trying to outdo their peers by bragging about an even more amazing story of what they once did. But the really funny part is that everyone's memories are faulty because they are now going senile, and they're relying on their "friends" to help them fill in the blanks! So while the hero or villain might really have a great story to tell, what comes out of their mouth ends up being VERY different. Each player has two goals - 1) To be the best at helping the other players in remembering correctly, and 2) To come up with your own memory/adventure that your peers agree is the best one of all! Remember When... comes with hundreds of unique cards, each with 4 words/phrases on its 4 sides. There are ZERO repeats, meaning there are over a billion billion different combinations! On the Active Player's turn they are creating a memory with 7 different cards, each representing a different part of the memory. 1) WHEN they did this, 2) WHERE they did this, 3) HOW they did this (i.e. Adverb), 4) The ACTION that they took (i.e. Verb), 5) The DESCRIPTION of the object of their memory (i.e. Adjective), 6) The OBJECT of their memory (i.e. Noun), and 7) WHY they took this action. For example, "Remember When ..., while looking for my other sock, in the crowded grocery store, I repeatedly kissed the furry caveman because the Great Conjunction was at hand!?" But the Active Player does not create this Sentence/Memory from their own cards. The other players are rapidly trying to assist the Active Player by submitting one card each. The Object and the Action Taken are determined first and read out loud, so the players have some context for their card submissions. Once one card of a type/color (i.e. "Blue") has been submitted then another available color must be submitted. As the players submit their cards to the Active Player, face down, they are trying to guess which of those 4 words/phrases the Active Player will actually choose. When the person building a memory matches the guess of the person who gave them the card, they both score a point. Once the Active Player has assembled their sentence, scored it for "helping points", then they read the completed sentence aloud (we suggest as dramatically as possible). This is because the other players will be voting on which memory of the evening is the most exciting of all! The person whose memory is voted the best at the end of the game scores two bonus points. Additionally, in the BGA version the last memory standing at the end of the game scores 2 bonus points. In the physical/home version of the game there are 2 winners at the end of each game - Most Points and Best Memory. The home version also accommodates up to 9 players, adds optional Orange famous personality cards in place of "the" , and comes with blank cards so that you can create your own. Remember When... occupies a unique space in BGA's library. It is a very easy, casual game where we hope that parents and children alike will enjoy just being silly and letting their imaginations run wild. Please see our latest tutorial, with the updated artwork by our friend Matthew Moeller. Thanks for trying the game out, and please spread the word! We are also actively seeking a publisher. If you have any ideas or contacts please let us know.

---

community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Played online. Why is this a game? Remember that game where you fold paper into a pyramid and write phrases on them then pick them?  Remember telephone?  Now give each player their own pyramid, and tell them they need to combine these phrases into a "humorous" story and thats it.    You can pick randomly without caring what the story is, as your not the one who is constructing the story and also it almost doesn't matter.  Its humour and storytelling value is so low its not even worth it; just buy a story game like Sherlock Holmes or that aladdin game at least you get some decisions

[Rating: 5/10] This rating may change with a higher player count.  Right now I've only played it with 3 people and it was pretty bland.

[Rating: 6/10] Designer: Eric Bridge Playing time: 30-60 Min Weight: 1.50 / 5 Publisher: The Game Crafter  [b]COMPLEXITY:[/b] Low. The rules set is very small, as it is appropriated for a party game. It can be taught in basically 1-2 minutes, and there is basically no learning curve.  [b]COMPONENTS:[/b] Low. The graphic design is quite simplistic, almost amateurish; and the different colors should have symbols to help differentiated between them, specially for colorblind players. Although it is a Game Crafter game, I have some pretty nice games from them, but they can only print what they received.  [b]DOWNT

[Rating: 6/10] A story-telling game where aging heroes/villains try to outdo each other's tales. Not bad, but other story-telling games work better with my game group.

[Rating: 8/10] Light-hearted comedy party game trying to come up with the most ridiculous or most awesome stories about what heroes and villains did in their past.  Rarely does a story fit together without some oddities in it, but when multiple parts agree with each others oddities it adds believably and humor all at once. A fun game to not take winning very seriously.

[Rating: 8.5/10] I have enjoyed playing this game several times and have had a lot of fun each time. I'm not typically a fan of "cooperative" games, but there's still an element of competition in the game so that makes it fun for me.

[Rating: 9/10] Full disclosure that I am the designer.  I wanted to create a fun and silly game that adults could play with children and have a great time, and I feel we succeeded.  My secondary goal was for children to LOVE reading, which is a vital need in our country, and this game makes reading FUN.

[Rating: 9/10] This game is fun for the whole family. There is a bit of downtime while waiting for the current player to put his sentence together, but I consider this as valuable visiting time with the other players.  It is easy to play and I especially enjoy finding the hints in some of the phrases to fondly remembered movies, TV shows, etc.  One of the best things to do to enhance your game play is to read your sentence with great drama!  This definitely ups your chances at winning the best sentence...if you can throw in some kind of special accent/voice with it, by all means!

[Rating: 9/10] Terrific game that can be enjoyed by the whole family or by friends at game night. Easy to learn and very very funny. Highly recommended!

[Rating: 10/10] This is a fantastic game! Very unique in theme and mechanics. It is like Mad Libs for grown-ups! I've played it several times on BGA. Highly recommended!

[Rating: 10/10] I've played this game countless times online at Board Game Arena and it's always a lot of fun.  Hopefully, the designers will be able to mass produce it at some point, as I'd love a real life version of it.

[Rating: 10/10] Love playing this game on boardgamearena. Would love to have a copy to play with friends. Such a fun concept of building memories. And I really love how other players can unknowingly throw each other off as other word. The sentence building mechanic adds so much more of a group dynamic than other word choice games out there.
